description: The plot illustrates accuracy metrics across different x-axis settings, showing three series labeled “Final Accuracy,” “Δ Accuracy,” and “Initial Accuracy,” each with vertical error bars. The x-axis is unlabeled and uses a linear numeric scale with tick labels from 0.91 to 0.99 at regular 0.01 intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0 with ticks at 0.2 increments. The “Final Accuracy” line is blue with circular markers and a solid line; it starts near 0.90 at x=0.91, rises to about 0.93 at x=0.92 and peaks around 1.00 at x=0.93, then stays in the ~0.94–0.96 range through x=0.95, dips to about 0.86 at x=0.96, and ends around 0.92 at x=0.99 after reaching roughly 0.97 at x=0.98. The “Δ Accuracy” line is orange with diamond markers and a dashed line; it begins around 0.55 at x=0.91, increases to about 0.67 at x=0.92, then trends downward to roughly 0.47–0.48 around x=0.93–0.94 and about 0.44 at x=0.95, drops to about 0.28 at x=0.96, rises to about 0.46 at x=0.97, then falls to about 0.10 at x=0.98 and ends near 0.15 at x=0.99. The “Initial Accuracy” line is green with square markers and a dash-dot line; it starts around 0.36 at x=0.91, decreases to about 0.27 at x=0.92, increases to about 0.53 at x=0.93, stays near 0.48–0.52 from x=0.94 to x=0.95, rises to about 0.59 at x=0.96, drops to about 0.42 at x=0.97, then increases sharply to about 0.88 at x=0.98 and ends around 0.77 at x=0.99.
